title: Marrow to marrow
hookLine: turmeric in warm milk at a sick child's bedside. one Veda turns from the great fire altar to rooms like that one
carry: caring for the body is sacred: prayer with remedy
last: OF THE VEDAS, THE ONE THAT IS SUNG.

lines: DOWN THE HALL TO A SICK BED.
cards: A saucepan on low heat. Milk, a spoon of turmeric, maybe a pinch of pepper, stirred until it goes gold. Then down the hall to a kid in bed with a cough and a warm forehead.
In some homes that cup is a remedy handed down from grandparents. Nobody calls it scripture; it's just what you do when someone you love is sick.

The Vedas we've read so far mostly stand at the great fire altar, with priests, hymns and melodies. The Atharva Veda walks down the hall, with hymns for fevers, wounds and broken bones. Today: the Veda of remedies.

teach.b: The Atharva Veda's word for a remedy is bheshaja: medicine, cure, what makes well. It runs all through these hymns. Some are addressed to fever, some to plants, some to a wound or an aching limb.
The healer speaks, the plant is given, and the hymn says what the healing should do. Listen to one, a hymn for setting a broken bone.

teach.h: MARROW TO MARROW, JOINT TO JOINT.
teach.b: In paraphrase: let marrow come together with marrow, joint with joint. Let what has fallen away of the flesh, and the bone too, grow back. It isn't abstract.
It names the body part by part, the way a person setting a bone would have to think, and speaks a hope over each, that it knit.
A plant goes with it: the hymn speaks to a healing herb and calls it rohani, the grower of the broken bone. So the hymn isn't a prayer floating above the injury.

teach.h: SAID AT THE INJURY, WITH THE HERB.
teach.b: It's said right at the injury, while the bone is set and the herb is given. That's the turn the Atharva Veda makes. The Vedas this path has heard so far sing to the gods at the great rites.

teach.h: AYURVEDA: A LIMB OF THE ATHARVA VEDA.
teach.b: This one sits at the bedside too, and it's where Ayurveda, India's classical medicine, traces its roots: the old medical books call Ayurveda a limb of the Atharva Veda. So the teaching is plain.

teach.h: PRAYER WITH THE REMEDY, NOT INSTEAD.
teach.b: In Hinduism, caring for a body is sacred work, and prayer goes with the remedy, never instead of it. A grandmother who says a prayer over turmeric milk and then drives you to the doctor is standing in that line.

how: The Atharva Veda holds hymns for healing fever, wounds and broken bones, often said together with a healing plant; its recitation is kept by Vedic chanters of its own schools.

games.q: what does “the atharva veda's healing hymns” mean?
o: Vedic hymns sung only at the great fire altar
Vedic hymns that forbid going to a healer
Vedic hymns said at the bedside, with healing herbs

games.q: the Veda of remedies — tap the pairs.
p: the grower of the broken bone

s: the Atharva Veda's hymns are only for the great fire rites
it also has hymns for the bedside: fever, wounds, broken bones.
one hymn names the body part by part: marrow, joint, flesh, bone
the bone-setting hymn asks each part to come together.
the healing hymns float above the body, never naming it
they're said right at the injury, often with a healing plant.

games.q: your little cousin's arm is broken. what fits the Atharva Veda's way?
o: say the prayer and skip the doctor
get the arm set, and speak a blessing over it too
skip the prayer: only the cast matters
games.why: the bone hymn was spoken right at the injury while it was tended, with the herb. prayer goes with the remedy, never instead of it.

practice: Move your attention part by part, the way the hymn does: feet, knees, hips, back, shoulders, hands, jaw.

Find one place that aches or feels tight and stay with it kindly, without fixing it, the way someone sits at a bedside, breathing toward it. If you pray, hold that place, or someone who is sick, in prayer.

wordCard.voice: The Atharva Veda's healing hymns. Bheshaja, remedy: hymns spoken at the bedside over fever, wound and bone. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: remedy, medicine. A word that runs through the Atharva Veda's healing hymns.

carryVoice: Your line: caring for the body is sacred, prayer with the remedy. Marrow to marrow, joint to joint. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Atharva Veda 4.12 (a hymn for setting a broken bone with the plant called rohani, the grower: marrow with marrow, joint with joint, flesh and bone grow back)
